My 3-line weekly review that took my output from chaos to consistent:

1. What worked last week?
2. What didn't?
3. What's the ONE thing I'll protect this week?

Fifteen minutes. Every Monday. Non-negotiable.

ChatGPT is only as smart as your context.

Paste:
— who you are
— what you're trying to do
— who it's for
— what you've tried
— what you want this time

Then ask the question.

Night-and-day difference.

5 "unsexy" AI income streams most people ignore:

1. Writing custom GPTs for local businesses ($200–500)
2. AI-powered resume rewrites ($50–150)
3. Auto-generated product descriptions ($500/client/mo)
4. AI-assisted Etsy listings ($20 each, add up fast)
5. Newsletter ghostwriting ($300–1,500/mo retainer)

No audience needed. Just skill + outreach.

Bitcoin's best feature isn't the price.

It's the fact that no one can freeze your account, inflate it away, or tell you what you can do with it.

Price is noise. Property rights are the signal.

I got rejected 47 times last year.

I also had my best year professionally.

Those two things aren't a coincidence — they're the same story.

You don't get wins without rejections. You just get nothing.

post_text:
The "2-minute rule" changed my life:

If a task takes under 2 minutes, do it now.
If it takes longer, schedule it.

Never "I'll remember later."
Never.

Three prompts I use every morning before my first meeting:

1. "Summarize yesterday's notes into 3 priorities for today."
2. "Draft the opening of my 10am meeting in 90 seconds."
3. "Pre-read this doc and list the 3 questions I should ask."

My calendar didn't change. My preparation did.

$97 is not a price.

It's a filter.

It separates serious buyers from people who'll never implement anyway.

Stop discounting. Start filtering.

DeFi in one sentence:

Banking, unbundled, running 24/7, with the rules written in code anyone can read.

You don't have to love it. You should understand it.

Confidence isn't "I know I'll win."

It's "I'll figure it out either way."

One is delusion. The other is identity.

I audit my calendar every Friday.

For each meeting I ask:
— Did I leave this with a clear next action?
— Did I actually need to be there?
— What percentage was decision vs. status?

Then I decline anything that fails the test next week.

Meetings shrunk 40%. Output went up.

The prompt that made ChatGPT actually useful for me:

"Before you answer, ask me the 3 questions you most need answered to give me a useful response. Wait for my replies."

Try it. You'll get a 10x better output every time.

Your first $1 online is 10x harder than your first $10,000.

Because you're not learning a skill.
You're shedding an identity.

The identity of someone who consumes everything and ships nothing.

If a coin's entire value prop is "it's like Ethereum but faster"…

It's not a thesis. It's a feature request.

Bet on primitives. Not optimizations.

You don't need permission to start.

You need a laptop, 60 minutes, and willingness to ship something imperfect.

That's it.

"Busy" is not a brag.

It's a signal that you haven't figured out what matters yet.

Stop trying to "replace" yourself with AI.

Start trying to replace your most annoying 90 minutes per day.

Once you free that up, the rest gets easier to automate.

Everyone wants passive income.

Nobody wants to spend 6 months building the asset that produces it.

That's why it's still available.

If the stock market closed for 48 hours, your 401k wouldn't notice.

If the crypto market closed for 48 hours, it would cease to exist.

Different promises. Different risks. Position accordingly.

The gap between "I should" and "I did" is the only gap that matters.

Everything else is noise.

Multitasking is a lie we tell ourselves to feel productive while being mediocre.

Pick one thing. Finish it. Then the next.

Boring. Works.

Prompt hack:

Ask ChatGPT to "rate its own answer on a scale of 1–10 before giving it."

If it says 6, ask why. Then ask for the 9.

Free upgrade. Every time.

The highest-leverage skill you can develop this year:

Finding people with money who have a problem they've already admitted to, and offering them a specific solution within 48 hours.

That's it. That's the job.

Everything else is ornament.

"But the chart says…"

Charts are great for timing.
Terrible for conviction.

Conviction comes from understanding what you own. If you don't have that, no chart will save you.

No one is coming to save you.

Which is terrifying on Monday.
And liberating by Friday.

The work is yours. So are the wins.

I stopped asking "how do I get more done?"

I started asking "what's the minimum I need to do so this week doesn't feel wasted?"

Six items. Always the same six.

Output didn't drop. Stress did.

Three underrated use cases for ChatGPT in B2B:

1. Turning meeting transcripts into next-step emails
2. Drafting Slack replies when you're too tired to be diplomatic
3. Rewriting your LinkedIn posts in three tones before you pick one

None of these are "sexy." All of them save 30+ min/day.

You don't need a product.

You need a reputation for solving one specific problem really well.

The product writes itself after that.

Bitcoin maxis are right about one thing:

Most coins are nothing more than "we're going to do what BTC does, but worse, with a tax on it."

Be picky. 90% isn't worth your time.

The version of you that will be grateful isn't born yet.

You're building them every day with what you do — and don't do.

Your first 90 minutes set the tone for the day.

Don't spend them on other people's priorities.

Guard them like a goalkeeper.

Most people use ChatGPT like Google.

The pros use it like a research assistant:
— Give it a role
— Give it context
— Let it ask clarifying questions
— Iterate

Quality 10x.

Freelance rate negotiation in one line:

"I typically work with clients investing $X per month/project. Does that fit what you had in mind?"

State the floor. Let silence do the work.

Undercharging is a worse problem than losing a bid.

post_text:
"When should I sell?" is the hardest question in crypto.

Start with: "What amount would make me feel financially free?"

Hit that. Take it off the table.

The rest is play money.

The truth about "overnight success":

It's usually 5–10 years of no one paying attention, while you built something worth paying attention to.

That's not a deterrent. It's the moat.

Cal Newport was right:

"Clarity about what matters provides clarity about what does not."

Figure out the one. The rest disappears on its own.

Build this habit:

End each day by asking ChatGPT:
"Here's what I did today: [paste]. What's the ONE thing I should have done but didn't?"

Brutal. Useful. Improves your judgment weekly.

$10/hr thinking:
"How do I work harder?"

$100/hr thinking:
"How do I work on bigger problems?"

$1,000/hr thinking:
"How do I build systems that work without me?"

You move up by changing the question.

Bull market rule:

If everyone you know is talking about crypto at family dinners — take profits.

Bear market rule:

If everyone thinks it's dead and you still believe — accumulate.

Simple. Contrarian. Effective.

The best time to do the hard thing was when you were scared.

The second-best time is now — still scared, just more tired.

Do it anyway.

I batch all my phone calls on Tuesdays.
I batch all deep work on Wednesdays.
I batch all meetings on Thursdays.

Monday = planning. Friday = review.

Not revolutionary. Just consistent.

Try it for 3 weeks.

"Write it first, then ask AI to critique it."

Don't use AI as a first draft. Use it as a brutal second reader.

Better writing. Protected voice.

1. What do I get paid to do that I'd do for free?
2. What am I the go-to person for in my circle?
3. What could I charge $100 for this weekend?

Answer all three. You have a business.

"Decentralized" is a spectrum, not a switch.

Coinbase is not your friend. It's a convenience.

Your keys → your coins. Everything else is a loan to Coinbase you can't recall.

Every time I've made a leap:

— It felt reckless in the moment.
— Felt brilliant 2 years later.

The same decision has two different identities depending on how long you wait.

Stop judging your brave moves too early.

Your to-do list isn't an obligation.

It's a menu.

Pick the one thing that would make the most of today — and ignore the rest guilt-free.

Build a "personal AI" by saving your prompts.

I have a notes file with 40 prompts I've iterated dozens of times.

Naming emails, planning weeks, summarizing calls — all done in 10 seconds because I don't recreate the prompt each time.

Your prompt library is compound interest.

Most "productivity hacks" are just people working on the wrong thing faster.

Before optimizing execution, make sure you're executing the thing worth doing.

Leverage > speed.

3 signs you're in crypto for the wrong reasons:

1. You check your portfolio 10+ times a day
2. You take financial advice from anonymous avatars
3. Your "plan" changes every week

Fix those first. Returns follow psychology.

The thing you're avoiding right now?

That's probably the thing that would change everything if you did it this week.

You already know what it is.

Go do it.
